question.problem:
Find the smallest natural number solution to the system of linear congruences below.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x≡1 & (\text{mod}\,2) \\ x≡2 & (\text{mod}\,3) \\ x≡5 & (\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since $2,$ $3,$ and $7$ are coprime, then according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $2\cdot 3\cdot 7=42.$

We will solve the system in two steps.

**Step 1.** Find the common solution for the first and second congruences of the system.

From the first congruence, we get

$$
x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,2)\,⟹\,x=1+2t,\,t\in Z.
$$

Substituting this into the second congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,3) \\ 1+2t & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,3) \\ 2t & ≡1 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,3)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $3$ is a relatively small modulus, we can solve it by trial and error. We have that $2\cdot 2≡1\,(\text{mod}\,3).$ So, we multiply both sides by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2t & ≡1 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,3) \\ 2\cdot 2t & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,3) \\ t & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,3)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $t=2+3s,$ where $s\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for $x,$ we get the common solution for the first and second congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =1+2t \\  & =1+2(2+3s) \\  & =5+6s\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2.** Find the common solution of all three congruences.

Now, substituting the common solution of the first two congruences into the third congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡5 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,7) \\ 5+6s & ≡5 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,7) \\ 6s & ≡0 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $7$ is a relatively small modulus, by trial and error, we have that $6\cdot 6≡1\,(\text{mod}\,7).$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}6s & ≡0 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,7) \\ 6\cdot 6s & ≡0 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,7) \\ s & ≡0 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $s=7u,$ where $u\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for the common solution of the first two congruences, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =5+6s \\  & =5+6(7u) \\  & =5+42u.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x≡5\,(\text{mod}\,42)$ is the unique solution modulo $42,$ and $x=5$ is the smallest natural number solution to the system.
